title: MentalThink: Reasoning Through Rendered SVG Sketches
hook: Instead of imagining a scene in words, this model sketches it — generating SVG code, rendering it, and looking at the result to check its own spatial reasoning.
key_points: Think-with-SVG: the model writes SVG code as an intermediate visual hypothesis, renders it, and inspects the image before continuing to reason.
Trained in two stages: supervised fine-tuning for SVG syntax, then multi-turn RL to reward iterative inspection and revision.
Scores 55.1% on VSIBench and 76.0% on MindCube, both spatial-reasoning benchmarks for multimodal LLMs.
Deterministic rendering makes the intermediate representation verifiable — unlike free-form chain-of-thought text.
content_html: Ask someone to reason about spatial layout, and they often picture it — a rough sketch in the mind's eye they can inspect and adjust. MentalThink gives multimodal LLMs a literal version of that: instead of reasoning purely in text, the model writes SVG code, renders it, looks at the result, and revises.
extra_html: The pipeline trains in two stages: supervised fine-tuning teaches the model correct SVG syntax, then multi-turn reinforcement learning rewards it for inspecting its own rendered sketches and iteratively refining them — externalizing hypotheses about object positions, geometry, and scene layout into a constrained, checkable visual workspace. Because SVG renders deterministically, the model's intermediate "thoughts" become verifiable in a way free-form chain-of-thought text isn't. On spatial-reasoning benchmarks, MentalThink reaches 55.1% on VSIBench and 76.0% on MindCube. Kangheng Lin and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: Look Light, Think Heavy: The Limits of Multimodal Chain-of-Thought
related.hook: Chain-of-thought should make models think harder. For vision-language tasks this study finds it's no free lunch — it can hurt perception, and models keep talking while they stop looking.

related.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
related.hook: Ask a big model to 'think step by step' and its math and logic scores jump. Reasoning was there all along — you just had to ask it to show its work.

flashcards.back_html: A reasoning loop where the model generates SVG code as a visual hypothesis, renders it deterministically, and inspects the rendered image before revising — externalizing mental imagery into something checkable.

flashcards.prompt: Why use SVG specifically as the intermediate representation, rather than free-form text reasoning?

choices.text: SVG renders deterministically, so the model can inspect an exact, verifiable image of its hypothesis
SVG files are smaller than JPEG images, saving compute
SVG is the only format vision-language models can generate
It avoids using any reinforcement learning

flashcards.explanation_html: Free-form chain-of-thought text can't be directly checked for spatial correctness. Rendering SVG code gives a deterministic, inspectable image the model can compare against its intent — plus RL training rewards revising it.
